Sampled HR@10 can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog HR@10, even in expectation; more repetitions do not remove this bias. Foundational results establish this inconsistency, while 2024 work investigates correcting negative-sampling rank estimates. Training margins therefore need empirical validation as predictors of the benchmark score; neither larger margins nor better full-catalog ranking guarantees improvement on its fixed 99-negative candidates. [Sampled-metric analysis](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/), [2024 rank-estimation research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371).

RecSys 2025 research evaluates sampling through model separability, agreement with full evaluation, robustness to exposure bias, and alignment with ground truth. A 2024 reproduction study also finds that popularity-bias conclusions depend on datasets, algorithms, user grouping, and evaluation strategy. These findings support reporting diagnostics separately by dataset and by target-item popularity, with popularity computed from training interactions. Observed popularity does not establish users’ conformity or diversity preferences. [2025 sampling study](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086), [2024 popularity-bias reproduction](https://ir.cwi.nl/pub/33989).

Suggested application, rather than an established guarantee: retain pinned macro validation HR@10 for selection; audit a fixed, budgeted validation-user subset against the full unseen catalog and measure checkpoint-ranking agreement. Report paired user-bootstrap confidence intervals for model differences within each category; obtain macro intervals by independently resampling users within categories and averaging the four category means. These intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and trained models. Validate diagnostic usefulness through controlled changes to loss, sampling, or regularization, checking whether diagnostic improvements consistently predict validation gains. Full-catalog audits remain supplementary; no test labels or evaluator changes are needed.
